correctness.rationale: After removing the common power of 2 from x and y, opposite parity would split the unique odd Mersenne-prime factor into two nontrivial odd factors, so the reduced bases must both be odd. The cyclotomic cofactor B_m is then exactly the Mersenne prime. For m=4k+1 and odd reduced bases, a complete modulo-8 calculation gives B_m congruent only to 1 or 5, whereas every Mersenne prime with exponent p>=3 is 7 modulo 8. The exceptional even perfect number 6 is excluded directly. All quantifiers and boundary cases are covered.
